key_insight: GeoABC makes neural operators boundary-aware by using geometry-conditioned anisotropic corrections that treat tangential and normal near-wall physics differently.
engineering_relevance: This improves aerodynamic surrogate fidelity where it matters most for design—near solid walls—helping replace expensive CFD with more reliable predictions.
method: Inject boundary geometry into intermediate neural-operator features
Apply direction-aware correction at the wall: tangential propagation vs normal constraint
Act as a structural prior compatible with multiple backbone models
evidence_signal: Across 2D airfoil and 3D car benchmarks, GeoABC reduced near-boundary relative L2 error by about 38% on average.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on accurate boundary geometry and may require careful integration with different neural-operator backbones.
paper_title: Geometry-Aware Anisotropic Boundary Correction for Aerodynamic Simulation
